title: From words to one next token
subtitle: A learning-first map of tokenization, vectors, transformer blocks, and sampling
footer: Use frame navigation to follow the mechanism. The outline.md file is the reading surface on smaller screens.

bands.heading: The whole pipeline
bands.deck: A prompt becomes one next token through learned transformations

visual.thesis: The model does not jump from words to prose; it transforms a sequence before choosing one piece.
visual.focus: Prompt → tokens → vectors → blocks → next token
visual.caption: One forward pass turns context into a distribution over possible continuations.
visual.explanation: Characters are segmented into token IDs, looked up as vectors, repeatedly contextualized, then projected into vocabulary scores.
visual.example: The phrase `cats sleep` becomes several IDs before any attention layer sees it.
visual.tradeoff: Every later choice depends on the tokenizer and vocabulary selected during training.

bands.heading: Tokenizer boundaries
bands.deck: Token pieces follow learned frequency boundaries, not human word boundaries

visual.thesis: Tokenization preserves common pieces and splits unusual strings into reusable fragments.
visual.focus: Why a word becomes one token or several
visual.caption: The vocabulary makes a practical compromise between coverage and sequence length.

nodes.label: play

nodes.label: play + ##ful

visual.explanation: A tokenizer searches its finite vocabulary for useful pieces, trading fewer steps against the ability to represent new strings.
visual.example: `unhappiness` may become `un`, `happi`, and `ness` rather than one unknown symbol.
visual.tradeoff: Smaller vocabularies create longer sequences; larger vocabularies consume more model memory.

bands.heading: One integer becomes a vector
bands.deck: An embedding lookup selects a learned row before position and attention are added

visual.thesis: A token ID is an address into a learned table, not a miniature meaning definition.
visual.focus: Lookup turns one ID into a point in meaning space
visual.caption: The selected row is combined with position before the first transformer block.
visual.explanation: The embedding matrix stores one trainable vector per vocabulary entry, so lookup copies a row rather than computing language from scratch.
visual.example: ID 314 selects one row; adding its position vector makes the same token location-aware.
visual.tradeoff: Nearby vectors often share usage patterns, but geometry is learned and never a dictionary guarantee.

bands.heading: Inside one transformer block
bands.deck: Attention mixes context, feed-forward layers transform features, and residuals preserve the stream

visual.thesis: Each block rewrites every token representation using context while a residual path keeps information available.
visual.focus: One block: mix → transform → add back
visual.caption: The final position is special only at readout; every position is updated inside the block.
visual.explanation: Self-attention mixes information across earlier positions, feed-forward layers apply a per-position transformation, and residual addition keeps the stream stable.
visual.example: A later token can use an earlier subject noun because its query attends to that position's key and value.
visual.tradeoff: Causal masking blocks future positions, so generation can never peek at the answer it is trying to produce.
visual.inspect: attention_mask[:, :, i, j] for future-token masking

bands.heading: From scores to a sampled token
bands.deck: The final vector describes a distribution; sampling turns that spread into one continuation

visual.thesis: The model scores every candidate, then a sampler narrows the probability landscape to one token.
visual.focus: Many plausible continuations → one sampled piece
visual.caption: A confident distribution is narrow; an uncertain one leaves more candidates alive.
visual.explanation: The last hidden vector is projected into vocabulary logits, softmax turns logits into probabilities, and decoding rules choose a candidate.
visual.example: After `The sky is`, blue may lead while gray and clear remain plausible alternatives.
visual.tradeoff: Greedy decoding is predictable; sampling can preserve variety but may select a lower-probability token.

bands.heading: Sampling controls change the shortlist
bands.deck: Temperature reshapes probabilities; top-p and top-k limit which candidates survive

nodes.label: Temperature
items: Above one flattens it and broadens variety
Changes the relative probability of every candidate

nodes.label: Top-p
items: Keeps the smallest cumulative set past p
Survivor count changes with model confidence
Trims the long tail without a fixed count

nodes.label: Top-k
items: Keeps exactly the best k candidates
Survivor count stays fixed every step
Can be blunt when confidence changes

bands.heading: Generation is a loop
bands.deck: Append one token, reuse prior work, and run the model again

visual.thesis: Autoregressive generation repeats the same forward-pass contract until a stopping condition arrives.
visual.caption: The sequence grows one sampled token at a time, while cached keys and values avoid needless recomputation.
visual.explanation: After a token is selected it joins the context, the cache supplies earlier attention state, and the next position runs through every block.
visual.example: `Hello` → `Hello world` → `Hello world !` repeats the loop with a longer context.
visual.tradeoff: Caching saves work for prior positions but memory grows with sequence length and layer count.
